title: Valentine's Day Board
h1: Valentine's Day Charcuterie Board for Two
seo_title: Valentine's Day Charcuterie Board for Two: Shopping & Plan
description: A Valentine's Day charcuterie board for two: triple-crème brie, aged Gouda, prosciutto roses, strawberries, raspberries and dark chocolate, with sparkling rosé.
hook: Red, rich and entirely intentional: a small board in reds and pinks that ends on dark chocolate.
why: Every color on this board is on purpose: prosciutto folded into roses, salami, strawberries and raspberries against the white of a triple-crème brie. It photographs well, but it also eats well, because the berries' acidity cuts the richest cheese on the board.
Aged Gouda brings caramel crunch and a little salt, which is exactly what dark chocolate and fig jam want next to them. Rosé Champagne or a sparkling rosé ties the whole red theme together.

timeline.what: Buy the flowers, berries and bubbles; chill the wine.
Take out the brie; make the prosciutto roses and chill them.
Add berries and petals last; pour.

faq.q: What goes on a Valentine's charcuterie board?
faq.a: A creamy cheese and an aged one, prosciutto and salami, red fruit like strawberries and raspberries, dark chocolate, fig jam, pistachios and thin crackers.

faq.q: How do you make prosciutto roses?
faq.a: Fold a slice in half lengthwise and roll it loosely from one end, letting the top edge flare out like petals. Two or three slices make a fuller rose.
Wash the berries and fold the roses up to a few hours ahead and keep them covered in the fridge. Build the board about 30 minutes before you eat.
